new_statements.quote: El acento es un signo que se utiliza para enfatizar la intensidad de la pronunciación en alguna sílaba de las palabras. Se acentuarán todas las palabras en aquellas sílabas que tengan mayor intensidad en agudas y esdrújulas, respetando las siete variantes que existen en la lengua tutunakú, excepto las palabras graves. [...] Las palabras tetrasílabas, trisílabas o bisílabas con intensidad de voz en la penúltima sílaba no se acentuarán y se les conocerá como palabras graves. [...] Las palabras monosílabas no se acentuarán. [...] Se acentuarán todas las palabras tetrasílabas y trisílabas que lleven la intensidad acentual en la antepenúltima sílaba, a estas se les conocerá como palabras esdrújulas.
new_statements.translation: The accent is a sign used to mark the intensity of pronunciation on some syllable of a word. All words are to be written with an accent on the syllable of greatest intensity when they are final-stressed (agudas) or antepenult-stressed (esdrújulas), across the seven variants of the Tutunakú language, except penult-stressed words (graves). [...] Four-, three- or two-syllable words with the intensity on the penultimate syllable are not accented and are called graves. [...] Monosyllables are not accented. [...] All four- and three-syllable words with the stress on the antepenultimate syllable are accented; these are called esdrújulas.
new_statements.citation: Instituto Nacional de Lenguas Indígenas. [2017]. Xalimakgatsokgni tutunakú / Norma de escritura de la lengua tutunakú (totonaco). México: INALI. 170 pp.
new_statements.locator: Spanish part, section 'Acentuación (´)', printed pp. 131-133 (PDF pp. 133-135); variant coverage incl. 'Del cerro Xinolatépetl' on map p. 79
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote: lines 4406-4519 (= printed pp. 131-133, section 'Acentuación (´)') carries every quoted sentence word for word ('El acento es un signo que se utiliza para enfatizar la intensidad.. respetando las siete variantes que existen en la lengua tutunakú, excepto las palabras graves'; 'Las palabras tetrasílabas, trisílabas o bisílabas con intensidad de voz en la penúltima sílaba no se acentuarán y se les conocerá como palabras graves'; 'Las palabras monosílabas no se acentuarán'; 'Se acentuarán todas las palabras tetrasílabas y trisílabas que lleven la intensidad acentual en la antepenúltima sílaba, a estas se les conocerá como palabras esdrújulas'); the ellipses only skip the example tables…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Only an orthographic statement, valid for all seven INALI Totonac variants (Cerro Xinolatépetl = tqt included): word stress may be final, penultimate or antepenultimate; penultimate is treated as the unmarked default and final/antepenultimate stress is written with an acute. No conditioning rule is given. Andersen's 2016 tqt lexicon (stress marked per entry, no rule stated) agrees: stress on one of the last two syllables (6 antepenult cases in ~750), nouns mostly penultimate, verbs in citation form mostly final, final stress on light and heavy finals alike.
new_statements.exceptions: INALI: monosyllables unaccented; esdrújulas listed as a marked class (e.g. wápapa 'sapo', táskuyu 'alacrán'). No tqt-specific exceptions discussed anywhere.
new_statements.domain_note: INALI norm concerns the orthographic word in isolation and is pan-dialectal/normative, not a phonological description of Ozumatlán Totonac; the tqt-specific evidence (Andersen 2016) is citation forms in a lexicon with no analysis. A first-hand analytic statement for tqt (weight- and/or morphology-conditioned, as described for neighbouring Northern/Sierra Totonac) was not found in any opened source.
new_statements.identity_note: tqt/west1511 = 'Totonaco del cerro Xinolatépetl' (SIL, INALI) = Ozumatlán/Ozomatlán Totonac = former 'Western Totonac' (Ozomatlán, Tepetzintla, Huauchinango, Puebla). Andersen's 2007/2012/2016 materials are first-hand tqt. The quoted INALI 2017 norm is pan-Totonac (all seven INALI tutunakú variants, Xinolatépetl among them) and must not be catalogued as a description of tqt. Beck's comparative work treats 'CX' as a separate Central Totonac language of uncertain (Sierra-Lowland-leaning) affiliation.

sources.note: Pan-variant orthographic norm explicitly covering the seven INALI tutunakú variants including 'Del cerro Xinolatépetl' (map p.79; Tepetzintla/Huauchinango in municipio list). 'Acentuación (´)', printed pp.131-133: words may be agudas (final stress, written with acute), graves (penultimate, unmarked default) or esdrújulas (antepenultimate, written with acute); monosyllables unmarked. Normative/orthographic, not a description of tqt.

Stress is marked per entry with IPA ˈ (e.g. chakatu /ʧaˈkatu/ 'cuarto', chachakg /ˈʧaʧaq/ 'rana', chapá /ʧa̰ˈpa̰/ 'lo muele', cha̱makxkúli̱m /ʧaːmakˈʃkuliːm/ 'arco iris').
